lessons.0.slides.1.title: 📋 Assessment Scope
lessons.0.slides.1.content:
This comprehensive assessment covers every module in the Level 4 Master course:

• M1 Burgundy History & Cultural Heritage
• M2 Global Premium Pinot Noir Comparative Study
• M3 Professional Sommelier Training
• M4 Wine Education & Teaching Methods
• M5 Business Cases & Market Strategy
• M6 International Trade & Import/Export Practice
• M7 Winery Management & Entrepreneurship
• M8 Expert Thesis & Comprehensive Assessment

The bank contains 55 questions; the system randomly draws 20. Passing score: 80 or above.
lessons.0.slides.2.title: 🎯 Key Review Points
lessons.0.slides.2.points.0: History and culture: Cistercian monks creating the Climat system, the 1395 ban on Gamay, the 1443 founding of the Hospices de Beaune
lessons.0.slides.2.points.1: Global Pinot Noir comparison: Oregon's 1979 Paris blind tasting, Central Otago's schist soil, Germany's GG classification, California's stylistic evolution
lessons.0.slides.2.points.2: Sommelier skills: professional cellar temperature/humidity standards, decanting timing, identifying TCA cork taint, wine-list structure planning
lessons.0.slides.2.points.3: Education and training: practice-oriented teaching, vertical vs. horizontal tasting, WSET/CMS preparation essentials
lessons.0.slides.2.points.4: Business and market: the Veblen effect, characteristics of the Asian market, margin differences between retail and wholesale
lessons.0.slides.2.points.5: International trade: sea vs. air freight timelines, tax rates by region, how En Primeur works
lessons.0.slides.2.points.6: Winery management: a new estate's payback timeline, the premium from organic certification, climate-risk management
lessons.0.slides.2.points.7: The thesis and master's path: MW dissertation standards, the professional blind-tasting assessment process, master-certification standards
lessons.0.slides.2.points.8: 🎓 Completing this assessment means passing the final capstone of the Burgundy Master program
